title: Rev1.5.3 Cognitive Task Memory

compatibility.policy: Clean break at the persisted Session boundary from Rev1.5.2: Rev1.5.3 adds task-scoped cognitive memory while preserving the Host-injected Provider architecture, Main semantic authority, Tasks/Investigation and universal physical contracts.

architecture.main: Sole semantic authority. Interprets immutable request plus authoritative request_context, freely chooses provider capabilities, user supervision, optional Investigation/Tasks, or completion.
architecture.runtime: Domain-neutral mechanical authority. Validates capability/result/effect coherence, confirmation, persistence, budgets and continuation identity; confirmed results always return to Main.
architecture.providers: Independent owners of domain mechanics and private runtime state. Providers register local capability IDs; Registry exposes provider.local canonical IDs and validates their physical contracts.
architecture.capability_contract: Capabilities self-describe purpose, inputs, returns, caveats, limits, effect class and confirmation. Providers may also publish establishes/does_not_establish causal boundaries; Registry validates their shape and exposes them without interpreting domain meaning.
architecture.actions: Exactly capability_calls, await_user, complete. Workspace mutation is workspace_transaction from the bundled standard provider, not a special Core action.
architecture.completion: Complete has answer, limitations, grounding_ids and effect_ids. There is no Direct/Observed/Effect classification phase. Main must compare requested world changes against actual effect resource, changed state and persistence; Runtime still checks coordinate existence/identity only.
architecture.effects: Universal physical_effect shape is resource, operation, persistence and changed. Main is explicitly taught that successful execution is not automatically task success and that temporary/isolated/different-resource effects cannot stand in for requested persistent/external effects.
architecture.continuation: await_user answers are retained as authoritative request_context for the same active task. Capability confirmation executes mechanically, records observation/effect, then resumes Main.
architecture.provider_context: Host injects Registry and opaque provider_context. Runtime/service does not import or discover the standard provider domain directly.
architecture.runtime_state: ExecutionContext exposes provider-private runtime state and generic cleanup callbacks; sandbox/container/session state belongs to the provider that created it.
architecture.configuration: Runtime validates universal host fields and delegates providers.* validation to the registered provider. Provider-specific search/sandbox/test limits are opaque to Core.
architecture.standard_provider: Bundled workspace/code/Git/sandbox provider only. Persistent cognitive Memory is a separate bundled memory provider.
architecture.semantic_freedom: Capabilities remain optional resources rather than workflow stages. Causal-effect literacy is generic and domain-neutral: no keyword router, forced capability choice or prose classifier is introduced.
architecture.contracts: Universal capability, Observation, Coverage and physical-effect contracts live below Core and Providers; provider implementations do not import eyle.core.*.
architecture.http_retry: Transient OpenAI-compatible HTTP statuses (408/425/429/500/502/503/504) retain retryability through backend error translation.
architecture.host_description: Host may expose opaque presentation/status metadata through describe(); Runtime passes it through without domain interpretation, while bundled CLI/Web choose which fields to render.
architecture.action_semantics: await_user means active progress is blocked on user input; complete means the current turn/task is adequately answered or finished and does not terminate the conversation itself.
architecture.task_memory: Task-scoped cognitive memory stores Main-selected EvidenceSpan coordinates plus semantic Findings and Conclusions. Raw Observation remains canonical and is not duplicated into prompt memory.
architecture.observation_replay: Physical Coverage memoizes external observation, while provider-owned rematerialization may project the exact requested already-observed range back to Main without physical re-execution. Physical coverage is not treated as cognitive availability.
architecture.presentation: Provider model projections report presentation completeness/ranges when a physically observed source is only partially shown to Main; silent source truncation is not treated as full cognitive coverage.
architecture.memory_separation: Persistent Memory provider remains separate from task-scoped cognitive memory. Task knowledge is active-task state and is not automatically promoted to longitudinal Memory.
